column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Entry says war of 1735-1739 (Austria and Russia v Ottomans); article gives Austro-Turkish War (1737-1739): war dates left out. Entry's Russia terms (Azov, Kabarda) not in article, not repeated.
Article says Abd al-Hafid abdicated after signing; kept. Article gives 'Treaty of Fes' spelling; used Fes in running text for the place, entry name Fez left to the site.
Entry says Italian troops ended D'Annunzio's regime 'the following month' (December); article says Navy, Bloody Christmas, no month except by name: left undated.
Entry says the Empire made peace at Baden 'later that year'; article names the Baden treaty without a date, so no date given.

Article calls the treaties a 'truce'; kept. Entry mentions the Grand Alliance; article lists England, Scotland, Spain etc. 'Historians treat' is my attribution of the article's unattributed claim about England's turning point.
Entry's last sentence (Peter the Great reversing it) not in article; not repeated. Entry date 27 February 1617 = O.S., article gives both.

Article says he discovered the islands; entry says 'sighting'. Article elsewhere says he never set foot on the island, used 'sighted'. Death date not given in article beyond c. 1540 so no 'Death' heading.

Entry says Florida Island; article says Ngella Sule (the same island group, Florida is the English name but article doesn't say so). Both kept as-is in respective places: I used article's name only in Setting - possible mismatch with entry, editor to check.

Entry says conquest of Chincha and much of Chile, not in article; omitted. Article gives the Pacific voyage 'around 1470' under his father; I did not say under whose reign. Death by poisoning is the article's account, unattributed there.

Article: 'ruled on his own from 1357' fine. Place of 1377 coronation disputed (Mile per Croatian/Bosnian historians, Mileševa per Orbini and Serbian historiography): entry says Mile; place left out. Bileća dated late August 1388 as the article has it.
Entry says Guatemala dictators and 1954 coup; the given part of the article does not cover this, omitted. Entry: dominated Central America and Caribbean - consistent.
Entry says Röntgen 'later taught' - consistent with article's list. Left out present-day rankings and enrolment numbers by rule.

Entry: died 682 or 683; article 683 (Vescera): death year left as 683 only in text - same as one of entry's options. Entry: reached Atlantic reportedly, Kairouan founded around 670: article text given has no founding date; omitted. Article says he entered the Maghreb at around fourteen (conflicts with birth 622); omitted. Article says dismissed 55 AH / 674 CE; left.
Entry says 'begun in 1104'; article hedges the same way. Article says workers 16,000 and 'nearly one a day', same as entry. Wood: Montello hills.
Entry says built in 187 BCE; article: work began after 189 BCE, completed 187 BCE; both in text consistently.
Article gives reign as 268-270 or 269-271; entry says 269-271; I wrote autumn 269 and early 271, which matches the entry.

'Both admirals died on that voyage' - article: 'With both admirals dying on the 1595/1596 voyage'. Entry: sighted in 1493 by Columbus 'traditionally said' - consistent. Entry's 'Spanish Town an early capital' not in article.
Entry: 1808 Prophetstown, 1791 St Clair near headwaters; those details not in given article, not repeated. Two entries of Vincennes French settlement not in given article.

Entry says 'signed in February 1922'; article: finalised 6 February 1922, ratifications exchanged 17 August 1923. Ratio: article gives 1.67 in Hughes proposal and 1.75 in treaty; used treaty's. Entry says 'lapsed after Japan withdrew in 1930s' consistent.

Entry says thirteenth century BCE; article gives death c. 1192 BCE (commonly accepted), radiocarbon 1254-1197; the death-year range kept, as a hedge from the article, may sit awkwardly with entry's century: editor to check. Entry mentions wars with Tufang and Qiang and 1976 tomb of Fu Hao: not in the given article, omitted. 'Fu Hao led a force of over 13,000 against Ba': article says forces up to thirteen thousand led by others under Fu Hao's command; wording 'under her command'.
No disagreement with the entry. Left out the manga edition of 2011 and the film Ghost Dog.

The article is mostly census data; the entry's mention of Ambala district formation, Buria and Kalsia, and industries is not in the article and was not repeated. About 270 words because the article offers little more.
Article's court section says Yanam was a Dutch colony before 1725, which conflicts with the entry's French post from the 1720s; left out. Left out recent politics and court details.
Entry says ruled 1494-1506; the article says he succeeded in 1495 and calls 1506 the 12th year of the reign. Accession year left out. Family list and popular culture left out.

Article gives no years for Hazor and Masada digs, so the entry's dates were not repeated. 'In office' covers his deputy premiership and party leadership. The article hedges Cast Thy Bread ('likely under the authorization of Ben-Gurion'); the hedge is kept.

Entry says Emperor from 1872; article says 1871 (and king of Tigray 1869-1871): accession year left out. Entry names the battles Gundet and Gura, which the article does not mention; not repeated. Birth: article gives 11 July 1837 but also says 1831-1837.
Entry says Gyegu was rebuilt after the 2010 earthquake; the article does not say so, so not repeated. Entry's claims about the chiefdoms are not in the article beyond Nangchen. About 330 words.

Article contradicts itself on death: 'died at 55 ... no direct historical sources' versus 'died and was buried in Kashgar, 1077'; the 1077 date left out and the hedged version kept. Entry says 'around 1069' (article: 1069 or 1070).

Entry says the Peace of Munster confirmed it in 1648 and says 'conquered during the Eighty Years War'; the article gives 1604 for the conquest and does not mention Munster, so only 1604 stated. The article gives a 2010 population of 106,522; omitted. Notable people list omitted.
No disagreement with the entry. Article says death July or August 221.

Entry says the town later passed to the Auersperg family from 1654; the article says it passed to the kings of Bohemia in 1569 and never mentions Auersperg: neither stated, to avoid contradicting the entry. About 300 words; the article is short.
Entry says forced to resign 'under communist pressure'; the article gives the allegation about his son-in-law as the occasion. Article is short; about 300 words.

Article contradicts itself on the end: deposed in 1091 in one place, kingdom overthrown in 1095 (and reign 1069-1095) in another; entry says 1091. No end date printed. Article's 'Overview' (Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics, legal and scientific claims, tolerance) is unsourced and looks wrong; left out. Left out al-Rumaikiyya and Zaida to keep within length.
No disagreement with the entry.
Article gives the death date as 1 December 1335 in the lead and the night of 30 November in the section 'Death'; only the year printed. Left out Hamadani's son, treaty with Delhi.

Article's mythology and early inhabitants are traditional; hedged with 'said to be'. Left out the article's 'rude and barbarous' description (Thucydides-based, 19th-century source) and its list of notable Acarnanians.

Entry says the Council was chaired by Antanas Smetona; the article's lead says Jonas Basanavicius, and the body says Smetona stepped down and Basanavicius was elected chairman in January 1918. Chairman not named. Entry's 'State Restoration Day' not in the article; not stated.
Entry says the embassy to Muscovy and Persia was 1635-1639; the article also describes a first embassy from 1633 (kept; no contradiction). Article gives birth as 1599 or 1603; no birth year printed.
Entry says the US assumed up to five million dollars of claims; the article says the commission distributed around five million, so I wrote that.

The article gives conflicting age bands (lead 7-12/12-20/20-30, body 7-14/15-19/20-29; leaving at 21 vs 30): no ages printed beyond the entry's 'seven' and the cloak at 12. Left out the 20th-century uses.
Article gives birth c. 20 September 835, matching the entry. Left out the report of the mother's remarriage to Bakbak (article calls it possibly spurious).
Article calls the hymn the 6th century Akathist in one place; entry says 5th or early 6th, so no century is stated except the scholars' 5th/early 6th, which matches the entry.
Article is muddled on Zengi's offices and dates (repeated passages about 1118-1119); left those out. Article's 1125 rebellion and 1126 confinement are given as it states them.
Entry says blinding and deposition; article says deposed then blinded; used article order.
Entry says he joined his father's trips as a teenager; article does not say so; left out.
Article dates the Troubadour Tower to the 9th and 10th centuries; left out.
Article's lengths vary (110-113 km); gave range. Left out entry's Frankish castle of Karytaina (not in article beyond the place name). Left out pollution assessment.

Article says Amarapura was capital to 1857 in the lead, but ceased 23 May 1859 in the history; entry says until 1859, so I gave only 23 May 1859 for the end. Entry says Amarapura 'served from 1842'; article agrees.
Article says Philip II appointed him commander-in-chief (anachronistic) and gives Breda as 1624 in the lead; I used the siege dates.

Entry says the Chalcidian League seized much of his kingdom including Pella until Sparta broke it in 379; the article says he allied with the League and later fought it with Spartan help; no seizure is mentioned, so I left the seizure out and told the alliance and the war. Article gives two reigns (393/2-388/7, 387/6-370) in the lead but only one expulsion in the body; I left out the gap.
Article's lead says another branch ruled 'until 1318', consistent. Entry mentions the loss of Cyprus; not in the article, so left out. Left out the disputed Wittek-de Jongh genealogy.

Article's lead says the dynasty ruled 'in the eleventh through thirteenth centuries' and gives overlapping dates for the Mardin branch (1101, 1106, 1107); entry says early 12th to early 15th; I used only dated events.
Article describes the Kyoto capture of 1333 vaguely; I followed it. Article lists his death as ending rule in 1358.
Article puts the exclusive turn in Year 9; left other dating of name changes out.
Article says 'As of 2024' for the archaeological state; written as 2020 dates. Left out the khanbaliq speculation.
Article gives his death as 16 May 1942 in the lead and 16 December 1942 in the body; wrote 1942 only. Entry says deported by the Soviets in 1940; article says arrested at the border.

Entry says the Baganda allied with the British against Bunyoro; the supplied part of the article ends before that, so it is left out. Left out the article's claimed descent from Bakiranze Kivebulaya, c. 400-1300 AD.
Article says he took the throne in 1266 but later 'ruled from 1265'; used the entry's 1266.

Thin article. Its lead says an area of 12,703 km2 and that after Vav-Tharad was carved out the remaining area is 6,176 km2 'remains the same', which is garbled; I gave only 12,703 km2 (as before 2025). Entry's princely states and Bombay State merger are not in the article; left out. Left out the 2006 backwardness ranking.
Article's two accounts of the battle are given as accounts. Entry says Lysander surprised the fleet on the beach; both accounts are consistent.

Article: battle on 4 August 1578; Philip II crowned Philip I by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581, entry says union of crowns 1580: Philip's crowning year left out. Article says Henry reigned 1578-1580. Ottoman presence on the field is disputed in the article; left out.
Entry says first major defeat in more than a decade; article: first personal defeat in a major battle in 10 years since Acre. Order of battle omitted.
Article calls Ferrand 'Ferdinand' in places; used Ferrand. Entry says Philip secured Normandy and Anjou; article says John handed over Anjou in a peace settlement: that point left out.
Article says the Company's victory was 'challenging'; left out. Entry says October 1764; article 22-23 October.
Entry says Bordeaux surrendered in October: article says French retook it 19 October. Article says debate over Talbot's death; left out.
Article does not mention motti or 'symbol of resistance'; left out. Article's Kiselev loss figures missing.
Rolling Stone ranking, Grammy Hall of Fame and CBS list left out (rankings). Entry describes Gerde's performance; not repeated.
Article gives 45,000 m2 (11 acres). UNESCO status in entry not in article.
Article gives reign 969-977 (in captivity from 971); entry says tsar 969 to 971: no reign dates printed.
Article has no human history; entry's Fort São Joaquim 1775 and the 1904 arbitration not in article, left out.

Article says 'founded in 1965'; entry 1965-1966. Articles says PMDB name until 2018 and elsewhere reversion on 19 December 2017: used the reversion date. Membership figures, bribery claim and critics' labels left out.

Entry says Henry I besieged the castle in 1102 and Æthelflæd built a burh; article gives 1102 only as the attainder and describes a mound: not printed. Article says elsewhere the town was founded in 912 by Æthelflæd and also not created until 1101: avoided 'founded'. Entry's sandstone ridge not in article.
Entry says Fribourg and Solothurn admitted 1481; article mentions only the Stanser Verkommnis of 1481. Article uses 'Morat'; entry 'Murten'.

Entry says fort is 16th-century; article says stockade 1591 and stone fort 1640s 'still stands', but also calls the fort '16th-century' in attractions: said 1640s. Entry says founded 1588; article gives no founding year.
Article mixes Operation PBFortune 1952 and PBSuccess 1953.
Entry says Guáimaro assembly elected him; article says only 'chosen' in April 1869.
Article says first Carnatic wars 1740-1748 in lead and First Carnatic War 1746-1748 in heading; used 1746-1748.

Entry says late eighth century; article gives no start year other than Charlemagne's time. Article says Insular script replaced in 11th-12th century and also 'not taken up until mid-10th century': used the latter.

Article gives two areas (10,293 and 11,815 km2) and 2011 populations before and after the Pandhurna bifurcation: no area printed; the figure given is the pre-bifurcation one. Entry says Deogarh rulers founded Nagpur and Pench National Park lies partly in it: neither in article.

Article says German protectorate declared April 1885; entry says German Solomon Islands from 1886: year left out. Article says transferred NSI except Bougainville; entry names Santa Isabel: not printed.

The article gives her death as December 1636 (text) and 19 December 1637 (lead); the entry says 1565-1637. Death date left out. Letter to Galileo year not given in the article; left out (entry says 1615). Wedding cost 'fourteen million pounds in today's currency' left out.
Article calls nationalization 'late 1960s and early 1970s' in lead and 1971 in text; used 1971 as the entry. Rankings, 'second deepest', production ranks left out.
Article gives Peter Colonna's dates two ways (1078-1108 or 1099-1151); left out.

Article's 2025 account uses loaded wording ('brutalizing', 'revolution'); kept to dated facts with attribution. Membership figures and seat counts as 'currently' left out. A date '22 November 2002' for the 12-point agreement in the article is a slip (2005); left out.
Article gives Anthony O'Flaherty/Henry Blake details and folklore; left out. 'Population is 32,000' kept as 'about'.
Article gives AD 212 matching the entry. Edward Gibbon point left out.
Article's lead and later text agree with the entry (1670-1723). Personal-life material (Cosimo's alleged relationships, Marguerite's conduct) left out.

SKIPPED: the saved article is about the city of Cyzicus; it has only two sentences on the coin (and calls the staters gold, where the entry says electrum), too little for a text on the coin Article: gold staters of Cyzicus a staple currency until superseded by Philip of Macedon; the cyzicenus worth 28 drachmae. Entry says electrum; disagreement, so skipped.
Article gives Cyrus's reign as 550-530 BC; entry says introduced under Darius I; consistent.
The entry's Tembe chiefdoms, Mthethwa and Zulu are not in the article; not repeated. Article says 'Praça MacMahon' beer trivia left out.
Article gives the diet's start as 23 January and 28 January 1521; start date left as 'January'. Entry says 'young Emperor' - consistent.
Article gives 'Doge Pietro II Orseolo' conquest 1000; consistent with entry. First doge Orso Ipato 'first half of 8th century' same as entry.
Article: built between 1307 and 1313; entry says completed c. 1313; used the range. Article's 'currently undergoing renovation' left out.
Article contradicts itself on the start of the diet-like details (Shanhai 27 May; entry fine). Murder-suspicion and Xiaozhuang rumours left out. Article's Guangzhou 70,000 vs Nieuhof 8,000 left out.
The entry says Daniel was crowned by a papal legate; the article does not say so, so not repeated. Article says 1253 consistent. Population figure rounded as given.
Article: premier four times between 1913 and 1918; entry says 'several times'; consistent. Bombing of Forbidden City and personal anecdotes mostly left out.
Article gives fl. c. 2450 BC; entry r. c. 2450 BCE. Article says ensi (ruler or king).
Article is short (315 words); text kept close to it.
Meissen 1710 in the entry is not in the article; not repeated. Article calls him German; entry Saxon.
Article says Northern Han conquest in 979 and also 'first three years'; used 979. Suicide of Zhao Dezhao and other anecdotes left out.
Article does not mention composition or patronage of music; omitted.

Article says he was deposed in the German revolution of 1918 (no month); entry says November 1918; month left out of text. Article's account of his private life and the divorce testimony is omitted deliberately. Article names the council as in Darmstadt. Wolfsgarten spelled 'Schloß' in article.

Entry says the first bridge was built in 411 BCE. Article says Diodorus reports a dike closing the strait in 411 BCE and that Strabo's bridge came at an unspecified later date; so the text leaves the date of the first bridge out. Entry says about 40 m wide; article 38 m at narrowest (consistent).

Article is inconsistent on settlement dates (Dilmun era from ca. 3000 BC vs first settled 2000 BC); text gives only 2000 BCE settlement by Ur traders and omits 3000 BC. Article's 2024 oil discovery and 2025 find omitted. Entry says 'Bronze Age outpost' and 'largely uninhabited since 1990'; article says a few residents remain, text says only that residents were expelled in 1990-1991. Article says Alexander's expeditions 324 BC; text attaches name Ikaros to that date lightly - the article places the naming under Alexander without exact year.

Entry says the mine's output was 'for decades the largest single source of revenue for the Swedish Empire' and that exhaustion of richest ores reduced income; the article says copper production declined without naming exhaustion; the text does not repeat either. Selenium: article says Gahn spelled Johann Gottlieb in one place and Johan Gottlieb in another; I used Johan Gottlieb Gahn.
Article gives dates in US form; converted. Article says the Association was signed 20 October and boycott from 1 December.
Article gives 1772 for the partition and 1773 for the Sejm's treaty of cession; entry gives 1772 only.
Article says the war ran October 1940 – 28 January 1941. Entry says territory transferred 'until 1946'; the article does not give 1946, so text omits it. Casualty figures omitted for length.

Entry says 'most were lost to the Byzantines and Ottomans by the fifteenth century'; text avoids that count and says many were captured between 14th and 17th centuries as the article does. Article mentions Parga ceded by the British in 1819 and Latin words; omitted.

Article says Brüx 1421 brought 'the ranks of Duke and Elector' but also says the grant came 6 January 1423 with investiture 1425; text gives only the 1423 grant and 1425 investiture and omits Brüx. Entry's 'heirs ruled Saxony until 1918' is not in article, omitted. Article has a muddled sentence 'Thus ascended Frederick IV, who called himself Frederick I'; omitted.

Article's lead says grand duke from 1858 to 1907; body says title taken in 1856 and brother died 1858. Entry says grand duke from 1856; text follows the body ('took the title in 1856'). Entry's 'responsible ministers, religious toleration and civil equality for Jews' not in article, omitted; article says civil marriage 'introduced'.

Article calls the sultan Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad (also 'Muhammed ibn San' and 'Ghori'). Article says the mosque was never always the largest; the Gawhar Shad complex was dynamited by British Indian Army officers in 1885 (omitted).

Entry calls him a Syrian Christian; article calls him Phoenician, born in Tyre. Text says only 'born in Tyre' and avoids the label. Article's consecration date hedged (328 traditionally, or 340-346); both kept as the article's own hedge. Dying c. 383 from lead.

Entry says the Sutagao chiefdom was conquered in the late fifteenth century by Saguamanchica, zipa of Bacatá; not in article, omitted. Article's 2018 census gives 138,498; an older 2005 census figure 107,259 omitted. Article says the town 'founded in 1592 by Spanish priests' in lead but by Oídor Albornoz in the history; text follows the history. Article says temperature 20 C in lead and 19 C in climate section; text says about 20.

Entry says Soviets captured him 1944; article gives two accounts (arrested in Bulgaria, held in Lubyanka, or surrendered months after the Communist takeover); text says only 'arrested in 1944'. His remains were reburied several times (omitted for length).

Article has no history section: Cartier's landing in 1534, the Mi'kmaq homeland and later settlers (all in the entry) are not in the file, so the text covers geography and economy only. Article is short; text is near the lower bound.

Entry says Council met from 1702 at the Casa de la Vall and that the 1993 constitution made it a full legislature; neither is in the article, so omitted. Entry says 28 members half elected by parishes: consistent with 14 parish + 14 national.

Entry says premier at self-government in 1964; article says the British agreed in 1963 to grant full internal self-government. Text gives no year for self-government. Entry says head of government from 1961 (article: 1961 to 1984 and 1989 to 1993). Entry says PUP 'founded in 1950' ok.

Article gives his birth as 24 May 1671 in the body and 25 May in the lead; text says May 1671. Entry says Anna Maria Luisa bequeathed collections to Florence; article says she inherited allodial possessions, so omitted. Article's accounts of his private life omitted.

Entry says villa built from 1482; article says plans from 1460, construction of the Kannon-den from 21 Feb 1482. Article's quotation from Rogers has conflicting dates (retirement 1474, lived there from 1438); omitted. Entry's claims about tea ceremony and ink painting not in article, omitted. Article says it 'is popularly known as Ginkaku' because of initial plans for silver foil.

Article says Kevin died about 618; entry only says 6th century foundation: no conflict printed. Entry says Vikings raided several times; article only says raids on the settlement and 1176 plundering by foreigners; left out.

Article calls him Duke of Terranova from 1502 in lead but the Viceroy section says made Duke of Terranova in 1504: omitted the title date. Article says Seminara 1495 and 'within a year' Atella; I avoided a year for Atella.
Article calls the region central Namibia; entry says north-eastern: not printed. Article says 'city' with 26,839 inhabitants.
SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance (a river course list and one sentence on the 711 battle); adds nothing to the description

Article says king of Hasding Vandals 407-418 then Vandals and Alans 418-428; entry says Alans joined after the Visigoths' 416-418 campaign. Article says 'Gunderic re-took the city in 428', unclear: left out. Article gives birth c. 379: not printed.
Article says Commissioner for Enlightenment and Public Instruction; entry says education: consistent.
Entry says the 956 law freed people 'wrongly enslaved'; article says slaves, mainly prisoners of war: printed the article's wording only.
Article says Kalakani was Emir 17 Jan-13 Oct 1929; entry says nine months and 'seized Kabul in January 1929': consistent. Entry says 'Nadir Khan' where article says Nadir Shah: I used Nadir Shah.

Article does not name a Dorian 'invasion' as historical fact; I used its wording. Entry says Aristodemus led the return; article says he was struck by lightning (or shot by Apollo) before the fleet sailed: I left out his role. Article says Argead dynasty 'so named because of origins in Argos'.

Article contradicts itself on rank: fourth in the Athonite hierarchy in the lead, third from the later 15th century: left out. Article says Nemanja was Grand Prince (1166-1196); entry says monk Simeon: consistent.

Article says the castle was founded with České Budějovice by Ottokar II; entry doesn't say. Article says Tudor Revival 1839-1871 and also 'Neo-Gothic'; entry says Romantic Tudor Gothic: no conflict. Windsor comparison in entry not in article: not printed.
SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of substance (a short lead, empty leader and election lists) and adds little to the description

Entry says the Brooke rajahs suppressed headhunting; the article says it was central 'until the early 20th century' and does not mention suppression, so I left it out. The article's headhunting treaty of 1843 'refused'. Article's 'Sea Dayaks' not discussed.
Article gives the sack of Ur as 2004 or 1940 BC; entry says about 2004 BCE: I printed no year for the sack. Article says 'Amorites submitted' in year 17 as an official year name.

Entry says 'early 10th century, probably from Isfahan'; article says tenth century, born in Rosta, Isfahan: I wrote 'near Isfahan' hedge-free but without 'early'. Article's 'sacred king' quotation is from the chronicle Al-Djarmi. Article lists the king's religious hedging as a story, not a fact.
Article gives reign 788-791 in lead and arrival in 789; entry says founded 789: I printed no accession year. Article says Tlemcen taken in 789 too.
Entry says 'sat paralysed until 33' and Pechersky relics in Kiev: consistent. Article says Pechersky born in Karacharovo; another version places Ilya at Morivsk (Lassota 1594): left out.
Article calls the remnant 'insignificant faction until 1931'. Bremen council government in entry not in the article: not printed.
Article text says the 1830 Act; entry dates the territory 1834-1907 and the Enabling Act was 1906 but statehood 1907: consistent.

Article gives birth c.771-790 and death 'late 851 or early 852'; entry says c.790-851: I printed no birth or death year. Article also says Pancorbo 816; entry says Roncevaux 824 ended Carolingian control: I used the article's hedge that his role in 824 is not directly attested.
The article says Champlain formed an alliance with an Innu group in 1603, matching the entry. Killing of two Haudenosaunee by Champlain in 1609 left out.
Article gives first-estimate and revised dating consistent with entry's 20,000 years. Entry says 'a lunar calendar' reading; consistent.

Article gives 'born 1967/1969' and names Khojayev; omitted. Dates 1998 consistent with entry. Entry says declared allegiance in 2015; article says Ghazi declared support September 2014 and leadership pledge mid-2015: I wrote only 'September 2014' and '2015 videos' — possible mild mismatch with entry's 2015; Sept 2014 left in, editor may remove. Entry says lost Namangani after 2001, consistent.

Founding dates: article says AD 980-983, entry says around 980; not printed. Entry says 'son Euthymius' and 'Byzantine emperor support'; article says second founder John Tornike: entry's wording differs (Euthymius is not called his son in article). Left out.
Article gives Bouchon 1725, Falcon 1728, Vaucanson 1740; consistent with entry. Entry says 'patented 1804'; same.
Entry says Nader Shah proposed 1736 (not in article). Article's Amman Message endorsement by Sadiq al-Mahdi left out.
Article says first President 1976-1977; entry says first president at independence; consistent.

Article contradicts itself: Jani Beg died 1357 (reign and lead) but 'after Jani Beg's death in 1358' in Legacy; I printed 1357 which matches the entry. Article says Berdi Beg returned to Sarai (confusing with Jani Beg). Entry says Jani Beg executed the Chupanid ruler Malik Ashraf; article says only that he installed a governor and Malek Ashraf controlled the region: omitted. Entry says 1346 siege: article gives only 'three years', so no start year printed.

Article gives her death as 4 September 1199 in the lead and 24 September 1199 in the death section: no day printed. Entry says Agenais as dowry; article says Quercy and the Agenais: dowry lands not named in text. Entry says 'mother of Raymond VII'.
Entry says suppressed coup 1924 and led forces from 1934: consistent. Son's death omitted.

Article gives Upper Belvedere 1721-1722 in life and 1721-23 in works list; entry says 1714-1723 overall. Left 1721-1722 once; editor may confirm.
Entry: ruled until February 1932; article gives 20 February 1932 as end; no conflict. Article says three children but lists four names: omitted.
Entry says 1880s Upper Senegal/Niger and Tonkin; fine.
Entry says Wedding Tower of 1908; consistent with article's Hochzeitsturm (no date in article).
Article calls Grijalva's discovery of Cozumel; entry says sailed past. Champotón (in entry) not in article. Short article; text may be under 260 words.

Entry says takeover by Nazi state in 1935 and Dessau works dismantled by Soviets; article says Hugo Junkers removed in 1934 and the company survived and was reconstituted: dates of takeover not printed, dismantling not mentioned. Check editor.
Article's phrase 'sixth century birth celebration' kept as given. Collector, rank and comparisons left out.

Entry says 96 km; article 95.68 km at opening, extended to 96.60 km in 1909: length not printed. Entry says over 800 bridges; article gives 912/969/988 bridges and 103/107 tunnels: counts left out, 'more than a hundred tunnels' only. Article says 2 ft gauge construction began; regauging date 1901 or 1905.
Article gives birth as 2 or 6 August 1929: no day printed. Entry says arrested as a teenager after Sétif: consistent. Entry's 'Nedjma drew on that experience' not in article.

Article's Toghrul/Yesugei passage ('Yesugei, having disposed of all Tughrul's sons...') is garbled and was left out. Conversion date: article says 'shortly before 1007' and 'early in the 11th century' and 'around 1000'; used about 1007 for the vision and early 11th century overall. Article says 12th-century Book of the Tower for an 11th-century event; kept. Language of the Keraites is disputed in the article; both views given.

Article's passages on his sexuality and drug use were left out (single-source claims, not needed). Article calls him 12th emperor of the Nguyen dynasty; not used. Entry says visited France 1922 and tomb near Hue combining styles; article only mentions the tomb as palatial, so the stylistic claim is not repeated.

Article says the khopesh 'fell out of use around 1300 BC' while also saying it was most common in the New Kingdom and changed from bronze to iron then (entry says the same); that date was left out.
